req.title: Return 404 for unknown routes
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-036 requires that any path not matching a defined route returns HTTP 404. The two violations were: test[0] had kind=negative but heuristic=EP (EP should be positive — it tests the nominal partition where an unknown path correctly triggers 404, which is the expected/positive outcome of the 404 rule), and test[4] had the same mismatch. Fix: change both to kind=positive since EP tests the valid equivalence partition (the system correctly handles the input class as specified). All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_unknown_path_returns_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
expected: Response status code is not 200, 400, 405, or 500
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_unknown_path_returns_404():
    r = client.get('/this-path-does-not-exist')
    assert r.status_code == 404
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.status_code != 500

test_unknown_path_returns_404()

tests.name: test_multiple_http_methods_on_unknown_path_return_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH requests to /nonexistent-endpoint
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: any path not matching a defined route returns 404 regardless of HTTP method
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_multiple_http_methods_on_unknown_path_return_404():
    path = '/nonexistent-endpoint'
    r_get = client.get(path)
    assert r_get.status_code == 404
    r_post = client.post(path)
    assert r_post.status_code == 404
    r_put = client.put(path)
    assert r_put.status_code == 404
    r_delete = client.delete(path)
    assert r_delete.status_code == 404
    r_patch = client.patch(path)
    assert r_patch.status_code == 404

test_multiple_http_methods_on_unknown_path_return_404()

tests.name: test_known_routes_all_return_non_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send appropriate HTTP method to each known route
expected: None of the known routes return 404
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: defined routes must not return 404 — decision table covering all known method handlers
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_known_routes_all_return_non_404():
    cases = [
        ('GET', '/headers'),
        ('GET', '/get'),
        ('POST', '/post'),
        ('PUT', '/put'),
        ('PATCH', '/patch'),
        ('DELETE', '/delete'),
        ('GET', '/cookies'),
    ]
    for method, path in cases:
        r = client.open(path, method=method)
        assert r.status_code != 404, f"{method} {path} unexpectedly returned 404"

test_known_routes_all_return_non_404()
